gap_description: No scientific authority in the repository for recommending a specific departure time or departure window for Malaysian Zone A small-scale fishers beyond what sunrise already establishes. Sunrise marks the Layer 2 governance participation boundary (g_t SAFE onset) under SDR-001 — it does not establish an optimal fishing departure time.
evidence_searched: Search conducted across: notes/ (111 papers), docs/implementation/dataset-label-derivation.md, docs/canonical/ (all canonical documents), docs/chapters/chapter-2-literature-review/, docs/canonical/architecture-illustration.md, publications/active/journal-1/research-design.md. Specific queries: departure time; optimal fishing hour; morning departure; fishing timing; tide and departure window.
evidence_found: dataset-label-derivation.md Section 6.3 EXPLICITLY DEFERS DepartureTime labeling to RQ5 fieldwork ('The full A_AI(SAFE) scope — including DepartureTime and Duration recommendations — requires additional domain expert elicitation or fisher interview data to label. These are second-phase labels deferred to the RQ5 fieldwork.'). Gao (2024) rates tide as highest decision factor (4.55/5) and notes tide-gated port access — this suggests departure timing is tide-conditioned rather than sunrise-conditioned, but no specific time recommendation was found. Yamin et al. (2025) documents trip duration of approximately 1 day and frequency of 3-6 trips/week but no specific departure time recommendation.
why_insufficient: No study in the repository specifies what time(s) Zone A Malaysian small-scale fishers should ideally depart. The tide-gating evidence from Gao (2024) suggests departure timing is port-specific and tide-dependent — requiring local tidal data not currently in E. Tide is not in E vector (documented limitation in dataset-label-derivation.md and appendix-c). Evidence that does exist (sunrise) is already encoded in g_t at Layer 2 and must not be reused without independent advisory justification.
what_would_close_gap: Primary: direct domain expert elicitation from Kota Kinabalu Zone A fishers about typical departure time practices and what time-based advisory would be useful. Secondary: tidal almanac data for Kota Kinabalu to establish whether tide-gating could provide scientifically defensible departure window recommendations. Tertiary: Malaysian Department of Fisheries operational guidelines if any specify departure windows for Zone A operations.
blocks: Population of DepartureTime rules in RS(SAFE)

gap_description: No scientific authority in the repository for recommending a specific trip duration to Zone A Malaysian small-scale fishers within SAFE state. Rahim et al. (2024) documents duration reduction under extreme weather conditions (West season: 30-40 kn gusts, >2m waves) when S = UNSAFE and Layer 3 does not reason. No study provides duration guidance within SAFE state.
evidence_searched: Search conducted across: all notes/ files (111 papers) for trip duration recommendations; dataset-label-derivation.md; docs/implementation/; all canonical documents. Specific queries: trip duration; hours at sea; maximum time; return by; duration advisory; safe trip length; fishing window.
evidence_found: Rahim et al. (2024): Duration reduction documented (7-10 hours → 3-5 hours) under West season (UNSAFE equivalent). Layer 3 does not reason under UNSAFE. This evidence is from the wrong state. Yamin et al. (2025): trip duration approximately 1 day (n=82 respondents) under normal conditions — descriptive only, not an advisory recommendation. No study provides a recommended maximum or suggested trip duration for SAFE conditions in Malaysian Zone A fisheries.
why_insufficient: The only duration evidence in the repository is from UNSAFE-equivalent conditions when Layer 3 does not operate (G(S) = 0). Duration evidence under SAFE conditions is absent. The daylight window (sunset - departure) is explicitly prohibited as a Duration basis without independent evidence. Trip duration in the literature is a descriptive behavioral measurement, not an advisory recommendation.
what_would_close_gap: Primary: domain expert elicitation or fisher interview data specifically asking about what trip duration advisory would be useful and operationally meaningful. Secondary: maritime safety guidelines for small vessel trip duration that could be adapted to Malaysian Zone A context. Tertiary: any DoF Malaysia or Marine Department Malaysia operational guidance on maximum single-trip duration for Zone A vessel categories.
blocks: Population of Duration rules in RS(SAFE)

gap_description: No evidence in the repository for recommending a Go advisory within CAUTION state. All three fisher studies (Rahim, Gao, Yamin) map CAUTION-equivalent conditions to restricted operations (Delay behavioral analog) rather than full operations (Go behavioral analog). No case was identified where fishers proceed without restriction under CAUTION conditions.
evidence_searched: Search across: dataset-label-derivation.md (all CAUTION rows); notes/ (all fisher behavioral studies); docs/canonical/appendix-c-formalisation.md (line 791 note on Go in CAUTION).
evidence_found: appendix-c-formalisation.md line 791: 'When S = CAUTION the Go recommendation is automatically presented by the system with a caution qualifier.' This passage has been classified as B (UI/presentation guidance) in Final Repair — it describes how Go is presented if produced, not that Go is mandated. However the phrase 'automatically presented' is ambiguous with a normative reading. The tension remains partially unresolved — OPEN-L3-3 created to track this. All three fisher studies (Rahim, Gao, Yamin) map CAUTION conditions to Delay behavioral analog.
why_insufficient: Fisher behavioral evidence (three independent studies) consistently maps CAUTION-equivalent conditions to restricted operations (Delay analog), not Go. appendix-c line 791 classified as B (UI/presentation guidance) — the statement describes how Go should be rendered *if* produced by rules, not that Go is mandated. However 'automatically presented' wording is ambiguous with a normative reading (A). Ambiguity created OPEN-L3-3. No study was found that supports a Go advisory under CAUTION conditions. The Go advisory in CAUTION state has no scientific justification in the repository.
what_would_close_gap: Domain expert elicitation: under what CAUTION conditions (if any) would fishers find a Go advisory useful rather than Delay? Clarification of the appendix-c line 791 presentation note: is this intended as a rule specification or a UI layer instruction? If the latter, no new evidence is needed — the presentation layer is outside Layer 3 scope.
successor_open_item: OPEN-L3-3 — CAUTION-Go presentation vs. rule semantics
blocks: Population of Go rules in RS(CAUTION)

gap_description: No evidence in the repository for recommending Delay within SAFE state when conditions are approaching but have not crossed the CAUTION boundary. The only dataset-label-derivation.md entry for SAFE state maps to Go label. No Fisher study documents a Delay-equivalent behavior within SAFE-classified conditions.
evidence_searched: Search across: dataset-label-derivation.md (SAFE state rows); Yaakob et al. (2015) for sub-SAFE operability concerns; Jeong & Im (2023) for sub-CAUTION restriction evidence; all fisher behavioral studies.
evidence_found: Yaakob et al. (2015): Boat A (6.54m) operational limit is SS3 top (~1.25m) — which is the UNSAFE boundary for small vessels under current thresholds. Boat B (5.03m) operational limit is SS2 top (~0.5m) — well within SAFE range. Sub-SAFE sub-conditions could theoretically trigger Delay for Boat B class vessels at o > 0.5m (which is still SAFE for small vessels under current thresholds). However: (1) the threshold 0.5m is for a 5.03m vessel which is at the extreme small end; (2) this would introduce a sub-classification within SAFE that adds architectural complexity; (3) no fisher study documents a Delay-equivalent response within SAFE conditions.
why_insufficient: While Yaakob et al. (2015) shows Malaysian small boats have operability concerns below the CAUTION threshold for their vessel category, no evidence establishes what Delay advisory would be warranted at sub-SAFE wave heights. The behavioral evidence uniformly maps SAFE conditions → Go.
what_would_close_gap: Specific operability studies of Sabah coastal fishing vessel types across the 0-1.0m wave height range, with behavioral data on departure decisions within this range. Alternatively: sub-classification of SAFE into lower-SAFE and upper-SAFE with evidence-anchored boundaries.
successor_open_item: No new OPEN item — sub-SAFE Delay remains absent from RS_candidate(SAFE)
